answer.rationale: Rollback is disallowed by compliance despite memory_b1's precedent, so the release stays. The bottleneck is the write path during peak settlement traffic, which makes route_read_replicas (read-only relief per memory_b5) a poor fit, and enable_circuit_breaker targets a failing dependency that isn't indicated here. Regional failover at write peak risks in-flight customer writes. Add_capacity directly matches the symptom (write-heavy peak, climbing p99) and has the strongest relevant precedent (memory_b3 headroom absorbing a surge), and it is reversible with no risk of losing writes. I verify b3 to confirm the scaling mechanism applies to write-path load, and b5 to rule out that the latency is actually read-contention on the primary, which would flip the choice.
